observations.statement: The original product surface exposed organisational work-habit and adoption insights to authorised administrators.
Microsoft publicly removed individual names and associated actions from the people-experience measures.
The redesign moved those measures to organisational aggregation and changed interface and privacy disclosures.
The announcement retained a score architecture and device-level identifiers for some technology measures.
Current Adoption Score documentation shows a continuing organisational product surface with eight categories and historical views.
No independent audit of tenant-specific prior use, adjacent analytics, worker consequences, or complete implementation is recovered.

open_questions: Was the correction implemented at the operative system boundary?
Were affected records, access, pay, duties, or accounts restored?
Was implementation independently verified after the deadline?
Did exits, silence, deterrence, overturns, restoration, and compensation enter later validation?
title: Microsoft Productivity Score: vendor redesign versus independent verification
